reasoning:
Nine files changed, and each one traces back to SEC-CER-001. UpdateChecker.swift has the fail-closed checksum guard, the quarantine xattr, the verifier hook and the cleanup on failure. DMGVerifier.swift is the team-signature check. The three Localizable.strings files each add the same three keys (en, pt-BR, es; every locale now has 23 updates_ keys, and there are no other locales in Resources). README, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md each get a doc line; after the change AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are byte-identical (cmp). UpdateCheckerDownloadTests.swift covers the new code.

The public UpdateChecker.init only gained trailing parameters with defaults (downloadsDirectory, revealInFinder, dmgVerifier). The existing callers are AiTaskbarApp.swift:21 and the Cadence/RefreshScheduler tests, and they compile unchanged.

The release contract still holds. Makefile:339 builds checksums-$(VERSION).txt with `shasum -a 256 $(DMG) $(DMG_ARM64)`. Both names are bare file names with no directory (Makefile:11,15), so they match the `name == assetName` check in fetchChecksum. That means every release published with make publish passes the new fail-closed guard. The dependency on make publish uploading the checksums file is written down next to the DMG naming contract in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.

The new subprocess (/usr/bin/hdiutil) is kept tight: absolute path, fixed argument list with -nobrowse -readonly -noautoopen -mountrandom, stdin from /dev/null, stderr discarded, a timeout that ends in SIGKILL, and a forced detach in a defer. It runs off the main actor in Task.detached, and it follows the same pattern as SecurityToolCredentialReader. It does not add a dependency, a host, a secret file or an entitlement. The download host allow-list (isAllowedDownloadURL) is unchanged. The validate.sh permission-check rule is about files holding secrets, and none are added here, so it does not apply.

The [String: Any] in mountPoint(fromAttachPlist:) is a local value from plist parsing. It never crosses an actor boundary and is not stored on a Sendable type, so the hard rule does not apply.

Hidden cost: the user-triggered download now does one mount and one full signature check. That runs off the main actor and is not on a hot path, so it is acceptable.

The mention of LEAK-FAN-004 (temp cleanup) is minimal and sits inside the same download path.
new_findings: INFO (SCOPE/release): the fail-closed guard makes the checksums-X.Y.Z.txt upload in `make publish` (Makefile:339-340) a hard requirement for in-app updates, but nothing checks for it. A release published by hand (e.g. `gh release upload` of the DMGs only) would silently turn in-app updates into 'updates_no_checksum'. Suggestion: have `make publish` check `gh release view --json assets` for checksums-$(VERSION).txt before flipping draft to published.

INFO (SCOPE/tests): TeamSignatureDMGVerifierTests garbage_dmg_fails actually runs /usr/bin/hdiutil, and apple_app_wrong_team reads /System/Applications/Calculator.app. Both depend on the host OS, so they run only on macOS runners. That fits this repo, but it is worth knowing if CI ever moves.

INFO (SCOPE/UX): when the team check is skipped on an ad-hoc build, only a notice goes to the log. A dev build will accept a DMG signed by any team, as long as the checksum matches. This matches the documented behavior ('skipped on ad-hoc builds'), and a follow-up could decide whether to show this in the UI.
